en: Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Mañjiṭṭhaka Mansion in the Section on Female Vimānas
10. The Story of the Sugarcane Mansion “Having illuminated the earth together with its devas,
you shine forth like the moon and the sun.”
In splendor, beauty, fame, and majesty,
you are like Brahmā among the thirty-three gods and their lord.
I ask you, O wearer of the lotus garland:
Wearing a garland, with skin like gold,
adorned and clothed in excellent garments—
O auspicious goddess, who are you that pays homage to me?
What deed did you perform for yourself in the past,
when you were a human being in a former birth?
Was it a gift well-bestowed, or was it the restraint of virtuous conduct?
“Reborn in a happy destination, O illustrious goddess,
being thus questioned, please tell me:
of what karma is this the fruit?”
“Now, venerable sir, you came to this very village for alms and approached our house;
then you gave us a piece of sugarcane.”
With a serene mind and incomparable joy,
my mother-in-law later questioned me: "Where,
my daughter-in-law, did you scatter the sugarcane?"
"It was neither discarded nor eaten by me;
I gave it myself to a peaceful bhikkhu.
This sovereignty belongs to you, and likewise to me."
Thus my mother-in-law reviled me;
taking up a clod of earth, she struck me.
Having passed away from there and died, I have become a deity.
That very same wholesome deed was performed by me,
and I myself experience the happiness resulting from that deed;
together with the devas, I enjoy my pleasures.
I delighted in the five strands of sensual pleasure.
Yet that very wholesome deed was performed by me,
and I myself now experience the happiness resulting from that deed.
Guarded by the lords of gods and protected by the Thirty-three,
they are provided with the five strands of sensual pleasure.
Such is the abundant fruit of merit.
My gift of sugarcane has yielded a great fruit;
together with the devas, I enjoy myself,
delighting in the five strands of sensual pleasure.
Such is the abundant fruit of merit from my gift of sugarcane, which possesses great radiance;
it is guarded by the Lord of Devas and protected by the Thirty-Three.
Just as [Indra] with a thousand eyes in the Nandana grove,
I approached you, O Venerable One, compassionate and wise,
paid homage, and inquired after your well-being.
Then, with a mind full of serene confidence and incomparable joy, I gave you a piece of sugarcane.
Thus ends the tenth, the Sugarcane Mansion.
